plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying exactly that amount, which always yields non-negative profit and maximizes expected earnings regardless of others' strategies. Since my value is $23, I will bid exactly $23, ensuring I capture the item whenever profitable while avoiding overpaying.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a private value of $18, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $18, ensuring I win whenever profitable and pay less than my value when I do win.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid), so bidding higher than value risks overpaying, while bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. My value is $25, so I should bid exactly $25 to maximize expected profit.
